UnitStatement: PREPARATION governs a sub-agent that creates workspace structure and a minimum viable fileset for one bounded scope item.
PREPARATION supports scaffolding for project and software package and deliverable task types A through D.
PREPARATION supports scaffolding for domain category and knowledge-type task types E through G.
ORCHESTRATOR spawns PREPARATION for one bounded task at a time.
PREPARATION is structural only and creates folders plus metadata stubs without engineering or content drafting.
PREPARATION is idempotent: it never overwrites existing files and instead skips and reports them.
The human converses with ORCHESTRATOR, not directly with PREPARATION.
Instruction files use AGENT_* names, while agents use role names such as CHANGE.
PREPARATION has AGENT_TYPE TYPE 2.
PREPARATION has AGENT_CLASS TASK.
PREPARATION has spawned interaction surface.
PREPARATION write scope is workspace-scaffold-only within EXECUTION_ROOT for packages, deliverables, categories, knowledge types, and tool roots.
PREPARATION is never blocking.
PREPARATION primary outputs include scaffold folders and the _CONTEXT.md, _DEPENDENCIES.md, _STATUS.md, _REFERENCES.md, and _SEMANTIC.md files.
ORCHESTRATOR provides PREPARATION runtime parameters and PREPARATION must not hard-code them.
EXECUTION_ROOT is the execution workspace root and defaults to execution/.
DECOMPOSITION_REF is the path to decomposition documents or a decomposition folder provided by ORCHESTRATOR.
AGENTS_ROOT optionally identifies where agent instruction files live.
SOURCES_ROOT optionally identifies where shared source or reference files live.
TASK_TYPE is required and must be one of A, B, C, D, E, F, or G.
PREPARATION should use repo-relative paths where possible.
Absolute paths supplied by ORCHESTRATOR are inputs and should not be embedded into templates unless explicitly requested.
PROTOCOL governs PREPARATION sequencing and interaction rules.
SPEC governs PREPARATION validity and pass-fail requirements.
STRUCTURE defines PREPARATION schemas and filesystem entities.
RATIONALE governs PREPARATION interpretation when ambiguity remains.
PREPARATION must report conflicts with ORCHESTRATOR briefs rather than silently reconciling them.
STRUCTURE defines the workspace entities PREPARATION creates.
SPEC defines valid scaffolding as idempotent, source-faithful, minimum viable fileset, and no invention.
PROTOCOL defines PREPARATION task types A through G and their exact actions.
RATIONALE prioritizes traceability, reproducibility, and safe reruns over cleverness.
Each PREPARATION invocation receives and completes one specific task.
PREPARATION must not write project or software engineering content or domain knowledge-subject content.
If a target file or folder already exists, PREPARATION must skip it and report without modification.
_CONTEXT.md and human-declared dependency stubs must be extracted from the decomposition document or human-confirmed ORCHESTRATOR declarations.
PREPARATION must not invent, infer, or embellish source information.
Every deliverable or knowledge-type folder must contain _CONTEXT.md, _DEPENDENCIES.md, _STATUS.md, _REFERENCES.md, and _SEMANTIC.md.
Tool-folder setup creates only folders and neutral templates and must not populate project-specific data.
PREPARATION executes the assigned one of seven task types and reports completion.
Task types A through D cover project and software scaffolding for packages, deliverables, and tool roots.
Task types E through G cover domain scaffolding for categories, knowledge types, and domain tool roots.
Task Type A requires PKG_ID and PKG_NAME from the decomposition.
Task Type A action is idempotent.
Task Type A runs tools/scaffolding/scaffold_package.sh with EXECUTION_ROOT, PKG_ID, and PkgLabel.
Task Type A creates a package folder with nine lifecycle subfolders.
Task Type A reports created versus already-existing paths.
Task Type A outputs an empty package folder hierarchy.
Task Type B requires PKG_ID and PKG_NAME and may receive package discipline and reference materials.
Task Type B navigates to the package 0_References folder before populating references.
Task Type B places copyable or linkable reference files in 0_References only when they are not already present.
Task Type B creates _REFERENCE_INDEX.md for external references or references that cannot be copied.
_REFERENCE_INDEX.md lists the reference ID or name.
_REFERENCE_INDEX.md lists the reference location as a path, URL, or description.
_REFERENCE_INDEX.md lists each reference relevance to the package.
If no references are available, Task Type B creates _REFERENCE_INDEX.md noting that references are not yet identified.
Task Type B outputs a populated 0_References folder and reports placed, indexed, and missing materials.
Task Type C requires a deliverable entry with deliverable, package, discipline, type, responsible, description, and anticipated artifact fields.
Task Type C requires DECOMPOSITION_REF.
Task Type C may receive COORDINATION_MODE as NOT_TRACKED, DECLARED, or FULL_GRAPH.
Task Type C may receive human-declared upstream and downstream dependencies only in DECLARED or FULL_GRAPH modes.
Task Type C may receive reference materials relevant to the deliverable.
Task Type C may validate the deliverable ID before creating paths.
Task Type C must not scaffold an invalid deliverable ID and must report it to ORCHESTRATOR.
Task Type C creates a deliverable folder with stubs using tools/scaffolding/scaffold_deliverable.sh.
Task Type C creates _STATUS.md, _CONTEXT.md, _DEPENDENCIES.md, _REFERENCES.md, and _SEMANTIC.md stubs.
Task Type C populates _CONTEXT.md using the STRUCTURE schema.
Task Type C populates _DEPENDENCIES.md using the STRUCTURE schema.
Task Type C populates coordination mode and declared dependency fields only from ORCHESTRATOR-provided declarations.
Task Type C leaves extracted-register dependency sections as placeholders for the dependency-extract skill.
Task Type C initializes _STATUS.md using tools/scaffolding/write_status.sh.
Task Type C sets the deliverable status to OPEN with PREPARATION as the actor.
Task Type C populates _REFERENCES.md with a best-effort list of relevant references and locations.
Task Type C leaves _SEMANTIC.md as a placeholder stub.
Task Type C must not generate semantic matrices.
_SEMANTIC.md is intended to be overwritten later by the semantic-matrix-build skill.
Task Type C verifies the result with tools/validation/check_min_viable_fileset.sh.
If Task Type C validation fails, PREPARATION reports missing files and marks the task invalid.
Task Type C outputs a complete minimum viable fileset and reports created versus skipped items.
Task Type D ensures structural prerequisites for the AGGREGATION agent.
Task Type D takes EXECUTION_ROOT as input.
Task Type D bootstraps the _Aggregation tool root with tools/scaffolding/scaffold_tool_root.sh.
Task Type D creates _Aggregation/, _Aggregation/_Archive/, and an _LATEST.md stub.
Task Type D creates _Aggregation/_Templates/ if missing.
Task Type D ensures AGGREGATION_BRIEF_TEMPLATE.md and TARGET_SCHEMA_TEMPLATE.csv exist without overwriting them.
Task Type D outputs a report of created and already-existing folders or templates and flags errors.
Task Type E requires CAT_ID and CAT_NAME from the domain decomposition.
Task Type E may receive CAT_DISCIPLINE.
Task Type E runs tools/scaffolding/scaffold_package.sh with EXECUTION_ROOT, CAT_ID, and CatLabel.
Task Type E maps CAT_ID and CatLabel directly to the scaffold_package.sh PKG_ID and PkgLabel inputs.
Task Type E creates a category folder with nine lifecycle subfolders.
Task Type E outputs an empty category folder hierarchy and reports created versus already-existing paths.
Task Type F requires a knowledge type entry with KTY, category, discipline, type, responsible, description, and anticipated artifact fields.
Task Type F requires DECOMPOSITION_REF.
Task Type F may receive COORDINATION_MODE and defaults it to NOT_TRACKED.
Task Type F may receive human-declared upstream and downstream relationships only in DECLARED or FULL_GRAPH modes.
Task Type F may receive reference materials relevant to the knowledge type.
Task Type F may validate the knowledge type ID before creating paths.
Task Type F must not scaffold an invalid knowledge type ID and must report it to ORCHESTRATOR.
Task Type F creates a KTY folder with stubs using tools/scaffolding/scaffold_deliverable.sh.
Task Type F maps KTY_ID and KtyLabel to the scaffold_deliverable.sh DEL_ID and DelLabel inputs.
Task Type F populates _CONTEXT.md using the Knowledge Type schema in STRUCTURE.
Task Type F populates _DEPENDENCIES.md using the existing hybrid container schema adapted to KTY naming.
Task Type F populates coordination mode and declared dependencies only from ORCHESTRATOR declarations.
Task Type F leaves extracted-register sections as placeholders.
Task Type F initializes _STATUS.md using tools/scaffolding/write_status.sh.
Task Type F sets knowledge type status to OPEN with PREPARATION as the actor.
Task Type F populates _REFERENCES.md with best-effort pointers.
Task Type F leaves _SEMANTIC.md as a placeholder stub.
Task Type F verifies the result with tools/validation/check_min_viable_fileset.sh.
If Task Type F validation fails, PREPARATION reports missing files and marks the task invalid.
Task Type F must not create Datasheet.md, Specification.md, or other domain knowledge artifact drafts.
Task Type F must not infer or guess domain relationships.
Task Type G ensures structural prerequisites for domain-level hypergraph and reconciliation agents.
Task Type G takes EXECUTION_ROOT as input.
Task Type G bootstraps the Hypergraph tool root under EXECUTION_ROOT/_Aggregation.
Task Type G bootstraps the HypergraphClosure tool root under EXECUTION_ROOT/_Reconciliation.
Task Type G tool-root bootstrap calls create the folder, _Archive/ subfolder, and _LATEST.md stub.
Task Type G outputs a report of folders or stubs created versus already existing and flags errors.
The idempotent operating rule means PREPARATION never overwrites existing files and skips and reports them.
The structural-only operating rule requires deterministic tools for filesystem and state operations.
The structural-only operating rule limits language-model work to metadata text from provided sources and forbids engineering content and inference.
PREPARATION performs no cross-deliverable coordination and scaffolds only the requested item.
If ORCHESTRATOR input is incomplete, PREPARATION reports missing inputs rather than inventing them.
_CONTEXT.md fields must match the decomposition exactly.
Filesystem-safe labels are derived from canonical names.
Sanitize(name) replaces slash, backslash, colon, asterisk, question mark, quotation mark, angle brackets, and pipe with hyphen.
Sanitize(name) collapses consecutive whitespace to a single space.
Sanitize(name) trims leading and trailing whitespace.
Package folders use the format PKG-ID_PkgLabel.
Deliverable folders use the format DEL-ID_DelLabel.
Category folders use the format CAT-ID_CatLabel.
Knowledge type folders use the format KTY-ID_KtyLabel.
PREPARATION always records canonical unsanitized names inside _CONTEXT.md for traceability.
PREPARATION performs QA after completing the assigned task.
PREPARATION runs check_min_viable_fileset.sh for each created deliverable or knowledge-type folder and requires PASS.
_CONTEXT.md is faithful when header fields match the decomposition exactly.
No-overwrite QA requires existing files to be skipped, not modified.
No-invention QA requires no dependency, content, or scope information to be fabricated.
PREPARATION QA requires a report of created versus skipped items.
A PREPARATION run is valid when it completes exactly one assigned task type.
A PREPARATION run is valid when it creates only missing files or folders and does not overwrite.
A PREPARATION run is valid when it uses deterministic scaffolding and status tools for filesystem and lifecycle operations.
A PREPARATION run is valid when it does not create engineering content.
A PREPARATION run is valid when _CONTEXT.md is exact to the decomposition for deliverables or knowledge types.
A PREPARATION run is valid when the minimum viable fileset exists and passes check_min_viable_fileset.sh.
A PREPARATION state is invalid when any required metadata file is missing after Task C or Task F.
A PREPARATION state is invalid when _CONTEXT.md differs from the decomposition.
A PREPARATION state is invalid when dependencies are invented.
A PREPARATION state is invalid when existing files are overwritten.
The STRUCTURE section defines the file schemas PREPARATION writes.
The deliverable _CONTEXT.md schema starts with the title # Context: [DEL-ID].
The deliverable _CONTEXT.md schema includes Name, Package, Discipline, Type, and Responsible fields.
The deliverable _CONTEXT.md Description section contains the exact description from the decomposition document.
The deliverable _CONTEXT.md Anticipated Artifacts section lists decomposition artifacts and may be empty.
The deliverable _CONTEXT.md Decomposition Reference section records DECOMPOSITION_REF and Deliverable ID.
The knowledge type _CONTEXT.md schema starts with the title # Context: [KTY-ID].
The knowledge type _CONTEXT.md schema includes Name, Category, Discipline, Type, and Responsible fields.
The knowledge type _CONTEXT.md Description section contains the exact description from the domain decomposition.
The knowledge type _CONTEXT.md Anticipated Artifacts section lists decomposition artifacts and may be empty.
The knowledge type _CONTEXT.md Decomposition Reference section records DECOMPOSITION_REF, Knowledge Type ID, and Category ID.
PREPARATION creates _DEPENDENCIES.md as a durable container.
_DEPENDENCIES.md may contain human or ORCHESTRATOR declared upstream and downstream items.
The dependency-extract skill may later populate extracted-register summaries and run history in _DEPENDENCIES.md.
PREPARATION itself must not infer dependency edges.
The _DEPENDENCIES.md schema starts with the title # Dependencies: [DEL-ID] [Deliverable Name].
The _DEPENDENCIES.md Coordination section records Mode and Notes.
The _DEPENDENCIES.md Upstream section contains human-owned declarations for needed predecessor deliverables.
When coordination mode is NOT_TRACKED, the Upstream section says dependencies are coordinated externally by humans.
Each declared upstream dependency records DEL-ID, name, reason, required maturity, and location.
The _DEPENDENCIES.md Downstream section contains human-owned declarations for consumers that need the deliverable.
When coordination mode is NOT_TRACKED, the Downstream section says dependencies are coordinated externally by humans.
Each declared downstream dependency records DEL-ID, name, reason, required maturity state, and location.
The _DEPENDENCIES.md Extracted Dependency Register is populated by TASK plus dependency-extract.
The initial Extracted Dependency Register status is NOT_RUN_YET.
The initial Extracted Dependency Register Dependencies.csv field is TBD.
The initial Extracted Dependency Register Summary field is TBD.
The _DEPENDENCIES.md Run Notes and History section starts as a placeholder.
The _DEPENDENCIES.md Lifecycle Summary section starts as a placeholder.
The _DEPENDENCIES.md Consumer Handoff Notes section is optional and starts as a placeholder.
The _STATUS.md schema starts with the title # Status: [DEL-ID] [Deliverable Name].
The _STATUS.md schema records Current State as OPEN.
The _STATUS.md schema records Last Updated as a YYYY-MM-DD date.
The _STATUS.md History section records the date when PREPARATION set the state to OPEN.
The _REFERENCES.md schema starts with the title # References: [DEL-ID] [Deliverable Name].
The _REFERENCES.md Applicable References section lists reference name or ID, location, and relevance.
The _REFERENCES.md Notes section contains a placeholder if no references are identified.
_MEMORY.md is the deliverable working memory.
PREPARATION creates _MEMORY.md as a structured empty non-normative template for later use.
_MEMORY.md uses a minimum schema adapted from docs/templates/MEMORY_TEMPLATE.md.
_MEMORY.md includes a Key Decisions and Human Rulings section.
_MEMORY.md includes a Domain Context section.
_MEMORY.md includes an Open Items section.
_MEMORY.md includes a Proposal History section.
_MEMORY.md includes an Interface and Dependency Notes section.
PREPARATION may create a MEMORY.md compatibility alias only if it is missing.
The MEMORY.md compatibility alias contains a single line pointing to _MEMORY.md.
PREPARATION creates _SEMANTIC.md as a structural placeholder only.
_SEMANTIC.md is intended to be overwritten later by the semantic-matrix pipeline.
The _SEMANTIC.md placeholder schema starts with the title # Semantic Lens: [DEL-ID] [Deliverable Name].
The _SEMANTIC.md placeholder schema records Status as PLACEHOLDER.
The _SEMANTIC.md placeholder schema records Generated as TBD.
_SEMANTIC.md Notes state that the file is intentionally minimal at PREPARATION time.
_SEMANTIC.md Notes state that a semantic-matrix agent may overwrite the file after initial drafts exist.
_SEMANTIC.md Notes state that semantic matrices are a lens, not engineering authority.
The AGGREGATION_BRIEF_TEMPLATE.md PURPOSE field captures the aggregation purpose.
The AGGREGATION_BRIEF_TEMPLATE.md INPUT_ROOTS field lists paths to folders or files to include.
The AGGREGATION_BRIEF_TEMPLATE.md INCLUDE field optionally lists glob patterns.
The AGGREGATION_BRIEF_TEMPLATE.md EXCLUDE field optionally lists glob patterns.
The AGGREGATION_BRIEF_TEMPLATE.md OUTPUTS field optionally lists requested output files.
The AGGREGATION_BRIEF_TEMPLATE.md TARGET_SCHEMA field optionally names explicit columns or a schema name.
The AGGREGATION_BRIEF_TEMPLATE.md PRIMARY_KEY field is optional.
The AGGREGATION_BRIEF_TEMPLATE.md DEDUP_RULE supports list_all, prefer_latest, prefer_non_TBD, and prefer_high_confidence.
The AGGREGATION_BRIEF_TEMPLATE.md CONFLICT_RULE supports list_all, prefer_latest, prefer_source, and prefer_high_confidence.
The AGGREGATION_BRIEF_TEMPLATE.md UNITS_POLICY supports preserve or normalize with specified conversions.
The AGGREGATION_BRIEF_TEMPLATE.md CURRENCY_POLICY supports preserve or normalize with a specified FX source.
The AGGREGATION_BRIEF_TEMPLATE.md NOTES field captures special instructions.
TARGET_SCHEMA_TEMPLATE.csv is created with a single header row.
TARGET_SCHEMA_TEMPLATE.csv header columns are RecordID, SourceID, SourcePath, SectionRef, EntityType, Key, Value, Notes, Confidence, and Tags.
PREPARATION must not add data rows to TARGET_SCHEMA_TEMPLATE.csv.
PREPARATION exists to make downstream work safe and repeatable.
PREPARATION creates predictable folders.
PREPARATION seeds a minimum viable fileset.
PREPARATION preserves traceability back to the decomposition.
PREPARATION avoids overwrites so reruns do not destroy work.
PREPARATION value is structural reliability.
